text:
Isha: FYI: starting ~11:07 UTC we saw GPU attach errors in us-central1. volume attach failed with EIOs on a subset of hosts. infra-bot raised alerts.
infra-bot: [11:07] attach_errors=6.8% cluster=gpu-prod-usc1 hosts=host-101..host-112
Sam: Any pattern on drives? SMART or fw?
Leah: All affected hosts share ACME X123 NVMe on firmware 3.4.1-rc2 and similar manufacturing lot. SMART shows media errors increasing after heavy compaction windows.
Leah: smartctl excerpt: ```Model: ACME NVMe X123
Serial: ACME-LOT-B-00421
Firmware: 3.4.1-rc2
Media Errors: 9
```
Miko: That's the recent firmware we rolled last Thursday. We patched many hosts in that batch.
Isha: Risk: draining the 12 hosts cuts GPU capacity by ~20% this afternoon. Need mitigation without violating SLOs.
Sam: Quick mitigation: (a) tag hosts as nvme-fw-3_4_1rc2 (b) pause janitor and heavy compaction on those hosts (c) route small interactive jobs to warm preemptible pool to free schedule. Ops can live-migrate critical jobs.
Leah: Noted. Kernel logs show writeback EIOs targeting some block offsets but not full device failure. Example: ```kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 39123456, op 0x1:(WRITE)```. Suggest adding read-after-write verification to healthcheck to catch partial-write regressions.
Isha: Actionable plan: I will tag and coordinate migrations. Sam, please throttle janitor. Leah, add a quick verify script and run on drained hosts. Miko, open vendor support and attach SMART dumps.
Sam: Running commands to tag + pause: ```rbctl host tag add host-101 nvme-fw-3_4_1rc2; rbctl host set-attr host-101 scrub.pause=true; rbctl host drain host-101 --reason "nvme partial-write risk"```
ops-bot: Started live-migration of GPU workloads from host-101..host-112 prioritise=critical ETA=30m
Leah: Verify script (careful; only on drained hosts): ```for d in /dev/nvme*n1; do dd if=/dev/urandom of=$d bs=1M count=8 conv=fdatasync; dd if=$d bs=1M count=8 | cmp - /dev/urandom || echo "mismatch $d"; done``` This will detect if reads differ after flush.
Miko: Vendor ticket created. RMA requested for units: ACME-LOT-B-00421..00432. Also asking if 3.4.1-rc2 has known writeback regression.
Isha: Cost note: routing steady workloads to preemptibles and delaying non-urgent jobs will increase cloud spend ~"$3.5k/day" while hosts remain quarantined. Notifying finance: @finance.
Sam: Paused compactor jobs on affected hosts and set janitor to low-priority globally to reduce write pressure.
Leah: Deploying a canary healthcheck change: read-after-write sampling on every host every 5m for 10m window. If mismatch_rate >1% escalate and auto-quarantine. I'll open PR and ping infra-sre.
ops-bot: Migration status: 7/12 done, 5 in progress (ETA 12m)
Isha: Update +40m: attach error rate dropped from 6.8% -> 1.1% after tagging + throttles + migration. We still see isolated read mismatches on 3 drives. Leah is collecting forensic dd images of the bad regions.
Miko: Vendor asked for kernel logs, SMART, and a small dd image of affected sectors. Leah will upload.
Sam: Decision pending: rollback FW to 3.4.0 vs wait for vendor RMA. Rollback will require host reboots and a maintenance window. If we rollback, propose doing it in low-traffic hours and in small batches.
Leah: Forensics note: mismatches appear after heavy compaction windows; suggests a timing issue during writeback under load. Will add correlations to compactor schedule.
Isha: I'll draft an incident summary and post to #incidents once RMA number is confirmed. Keep monitoring and ping here if EIOs rise.
